title: fix(formula): a bare date ordering before a record. date arithmetic still slips past the flow-condition refusal (follow-up of #36333)
body:
repo:objectstack#4 · os-project-manager · session_01FEkQ5pb2t8Z8C64PkPyVt1

Follow-up of PR #36333 (#34946), carried from contract review 7076631700 S1 (should-fix, non-blocking) and its nits N1–N3. Filed under the maintainer's 2026-11-22 07:49Z rule that should-fix items go to their own card.

**S1 (by code read, not yet run; measure first).** A flow condition that orders a bare date field against a text literal AND-ed before a root read's date arithmetic, e.g. `due_date > "2026-01-01" && record.due_date + 1 > 5`, is accepted, though it faults on every run. In `packages/formula/src/cel-engine.ts` the bare pass meets the Timestamp-vs-string ordering first and `confirmAgainstDateText` stands it down; the record-root pass types bare names and roots together (`buildTypedEnv(bareTypes, 'flattened', …)`), meets the same ordering first, sees it is not `isDateArith` and answers null; `recordRootDateTextIssue` then asks `recordRootReadsFaultDateArith`, which types the roots alone, meets `record.due_date + 1` first and stands down as "answered by `firstTypeMismatch`". All-root and all-bare spellings are refused; only the mixed one falls through. Not a regression (`main` accepts it too).
Fix direction from the review: when the root pass's first fault is not date arithmetic, also ask the roots-only typing, or have the stand-down ask `firstTypeMismatch`'s actual answer.

**Nits (same card, optional):**
- N1: `offendingRecordRead` names the first Timestamp field read through a root in field-map order, which can be a read other than the one in the arithmetic.
- N2: a bare-and-root pair under unproven names reports the bare verdict at `run-may-fail`.
- N3: the #30025 swap in `validate.ts` `typeSoundnessIssue` can now return a root `date-arith`; no pin names it.

Done when: S1 measured; if confirmed, the mixed spelling is refused at `os validate` and the publish door like the other two, pinned with an ablation; nits pinned or split off. Narrowing (newly refused) ⇒ declare it as #36333 did.
